record.paper_title: Open problems in microscopic theory of large-amplitude collective motion
record.original_question: What non-perturbative microscopic framework can describe large-amplitude collective motion in odd-A nuclei, or more generally in systems with several quasiparticles present, while treating the interplay between single-particle motion and collective motion in a unified way rather than starting from a small-amplitude particle-vibration-coupling approximation?

evidence.quote: In fact, microscopic description of LACM in odd-A nuclei remains as a vast unexplored field.
Non-perturbative method capable of treating LACM in odd-A nuclei (generally speaking, LACM in the presence of several quasiparticles) is lacking, however.

artifact.status_search_result: The microscopic description of large-amplitude collective motion in odd-A nuclei is widely acknowledged as a largely unexplored area. Recent work has extended non-perturbative LACM tools (ASCC, ATDHFB, GCM) primarily for even-even systems, with progress on odd-A nuclei mostly via particle–vibration coupling or projection/blocking on top of mean-field calculations rather than a unified non-perturbative LACM framework. No comprehensive non-perturbative LACM theory for odd-A or multi-quasiparticle systems satisfying all the stated criteria appears to have been established.
